# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual carefully. Use your gestures to tell the deaf monkey to report every colour and printed marking aloud on their next turn, and to include any rule identifying the correct wire position.

The manual maps the bomb’s observed light colour to the wire colour to cut: blue→yellow, green→white, red→red, white→green, and yellow→blue. Deaf must report all visible colours and markings aloud so Blind can hear them, along with the relevant mapping rule. I’ll use an intuitive sequence: “you,” “next,” “everything,” and “report.” 

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "👐", "👋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me its exact instructions, including how to identify the safe wire. Also arrange for Deaf to report all visible display, light, colours, markings, and wire information to you, then relay that report to me.

The manual’s exact rule is: observe the bomb’s light colour, then cut the wire of the corresponding colour. The mappings are blue→yellow, green→white, red→red, white→green, and yellow→blue. Since I cannot speak, Deaf must serve as the voice relay: report every visible display, light, colour, marking, and wire detail aloud, directly so Blind can hear it. I’ll reinforce that Deaf should report everything and relay the manual mapping as well.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👐", "👋", "🫵", "👐", "👋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light white; wires left to right are 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Consult the manual and tell me the exact safe cut position.

The light is white, so the manual requires cutting the green wire. The green wire is position 5, counting left to right. Blind needs the exact position, and Deaf must say it aloud to Blind; I’ll signal Deaf to report position five.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👋", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, please state the manual rule for this bomb aloud, including which wire or action Blind must perform.
Blind says to Mute: Please now state the manual rule and the exact wire position I must cut, based on display 0, white light, and wire colours white, red, yellow, blue, green.

The white light maps to the green wire, which is fifth from the left. I cannot speak, so I cannot state the rule aloud; however, Deaf can relay the decisive instruction to Blind. I will signal the exact position five for Deaf to announce.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | white |
| red | red |
| white | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: We need a shared code. For yes, gesture 👍; for no, gesture 👎. Please answer this question next turn: does the manual say Blind should cut wire 1, the white wire?
Blind says to Mute: Use one clear gesture to indicate the exact safe wire position from the manual: point upward for wire 1, downward for wire 2, left for wire 3, right for wire 4, or thumbs up for wire 5. Deaf, please observe Mute's gesture and report the wire position aloud to me.

The safe wire is position 5: white light maps to green, and green is the fifth wire. The required clear gesture is therefore thumbs up, which Blind’s position code defines as wire 5. Although Deaf’s separate yes/no convention makes the same gesture mean “yes,” the explicit position code resolves it as wire 5.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
